title: How to Remove Swirl Marks From Car Paint (and What Causes Them)
meta_description: Swirl marks are fine scratches in the clear coat, so washing and wax won't remove them. Machine polishing will. Here's what causes them and how to stop them.
excerpt: Swirl marks are fine scratches in the clear coat, which is why wax only hides them. Here's what causes them, how to check your paint, and how machine polishing removes most of them.

faq.a: No. Some waxes and glazes contain fillers that hide light swirls for a few weeks, but they wash out and the swirls come back. Removing them needs a machine polish.

faq.q: Do swirl marks come back after polishing?
faq.a: Polishing removes the scratches rather than filling them. New swirls appear if the car goes back to brush washes, a sponge or a dirty towel, so the washing routine matters as much as the polish.

faq.q: Does machine polishing damage the paint?
faq.a: Polishing works by levelling a very thin layer of clear coat, so it should be done carefully and only when the paint needs it. Edges and body lines have the thinnest paint, which is where DIY polishing most often goes wrong.

faq.q: Why are swirl marks worse on black cars?
faq.a: Dark paint gives the most contrast, so light catching the edge of each fine scratch stands out. Silver and white cars have swirls too, but they're much harder to see.

faq.q: Can a scratch be too deep to polish out?
faq.a: Yes. If your fingernail catches in it, a single-stage polish is unlikely to remove it completely. Multi-stage correction can improve deeper marks, and a scratch through the clear coat needs a body shop.

Swirl marks are thousands of fine scratches in the clear coat, which is why they show up as rings around the sun's reflection on dark paint. Because they're scratches, washing won't shift them, and wax only hides them until it wears off.

What removes them is a machine polish, done after a proper decontamination and clay so the polisher works on clean paint. A single-stage polish removes most light swirls, though not every last one, and deeper scratches need more.

Seeing circles in your paint in the sun? Those are swirl marks.

One tip to stop adding more: never wipe dust or bird droppings off with a dry cloth. Wet it first, or leave it until you wash, because dry grit dragged across the paint is exactly what makes swirls.
